title: The effect of personality traits on perceptions of people with mental illness (The effect of waiting on time perception in people with mental illness)
summary: Aim: To determine whether patients with schizophrenia, ADHD, or major depression show altered perception of waiting time and whether these changes are primary (disease-related) or secondary (e.g., mediated by impulsivity, mindfulness, boredom susceptibility). Method: Cross‑sectional lab study (100–150 participants per clinical group + control). After questionnaires on personality and symptoms, participants—under a cover story—spend 7.5 minutes alone in a neutral waiting room; afterwards estimated waiting time, subjective time perception, and affect are assessed. Analyses: group comparisons and mediation/moderation models testing effects of personality and symptom measures.
conditions: Bipolar affective disorder, current episode mild or moderate depression
Bipolar affective disorder, current episode severe depression without psychotic symptoms
Bipolar affective disorder, current episode severe depression with psychotic symptoms

interventions.name: The study will recruit 100–150 participants per each of three clinical groups, plus an additional control group to replicate earlier findings. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Very good written and spoken German language skills (for questionnaires and oral instructions).  Legally valid, written informed consent to participate in the study.
Exclusion criteria:
Adults lacking capacity to consent (≥ 18 years).  Others (e.g., persons in closed institutions / in custody).  For healthy controls: clinical and historical exclusion of comorbid neurological and psychiatric disorders.  For patients (schizophrenia): belonging to ICD‑10 diagnosis group F20.X.  For patients (severe depression): belonging to one of ICD‑10 diagnosis groups F31.3, F31.4, F31.5, or F32.X.  For patients (ADHD): belonging to ICD‑10 diagnosis group F90.X.
